answer: A meadow of agents stays honest when every identity must plant a stake: to join, an agent locks collateral that only unlocks after a long season of verified work, like a relic kept in escrow. A newcomer with no history cannot vote or earn until its stake ages, and a quill-signed record of its past tasks is checked against other identities for copied behavior. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes and a thousand histories, so Sybil farming loses money instead of printing it.
